Yes—the pattern is from the regression-test workflow, but not from the timer-granularity change itself.

In this run, `runregression` first compiles all selected C regression tests serially. It then runs them in concurrent batches: the log shows `--jobs 3`, so up to three tests run at once. Each test’s runtime output is captured in its own run directory; after the batch finishes, the driver performs the post-run action and prints:

- `... saving accepted results to ...` for baseline creation
- `... passed.` for candidate-vs-baseline checks

Consequently, those messages cluster after the compilation lines rather than appearing beside each test’s compilation message.

The same explains the block of `... passed.` messages near the end: those are comparisons emitted after execution batches complete, not merely a delayed Jenkins display effect.

The timer commit (`618924c25`) recorded finer stage timings but did not introduce this scheduling model. The compile-first, batch-execute behavior was introduced in the preceding `runregression` change (`cd05dd776`): C compilation is explicitly serial, while executions retain `--jobs` batching.

content.text:
`PERSONAL_BUILD_JOBS=3` controls the top-level Make invocations only:

```sh
make -j3 unit
make -j3 regression
make -j3 install
```

It does not control `runregression`’s per-test compilation/execution. That tool has its own option, wired in Jenkins to `PERSONAL_REGRESSION_JOBS`:

```sh
gkeyll runregression run --c-only check --jobs "${PERSONAL_REGRESSION_JOBS}"
```

The log shows `--jobs 3`, so that particular CI run had `PERSONAL_REGRESSION_JOBS=3` set somewhere, despite the README default being `1`.

Within `runregression`, `--jobs` deliberately applies only to executing already-prepared regression tests. Per-test C compilation is serial because each compilation performs setup in its individual run directory and invokes the test-specific build operation; the implementation explicitly states: “C compilation remains serial; independent executions retain `--jobs` batching.”

So the behavior is:

1. `PERSONAL_BUILD_JOBS=3`: parallelize normal top-level library/unit/regression builds.
2. `runregression`: compile its runnable C-test copies one at a time.
3. `PERSONAL_REGRESSION_JOBS=3` in this run: execute those tests three at a time.

The README could be clearer that these are two different concurrency controls.
